subs.label: Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by what the everyday life is organised around: a healing mood, a cute ensemble, a club, a stage, food, a job or a household.

leaves.label: Iyashikei
leaves.defn: A series or film whose purpose is to soothe: unhurried days, gentle landscapes and an absence of real conflict carry it (Aria the Animation, Non Non Biyori, Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou, Yuru Camp). If the healing comes mainly from a cast of cute girls bantering, it goes to C6-2; if from food, C6-7.
leaves.see: C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things; C6-7 Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.axis: by what does the soothing: countryside and sea, a fantastical or after-the-end world, a pet, the road or the campsite

leaves.label: Cute Girls Doing Cute Things
leaves.defn: An ensemble of (usually) teenage girls whose small daily pleasures and banter are the whole story, usually adapted from a four-panel manga (Azumanga Daiou, K-On!, Kiniro Mosaic, Gochuumon wa Usagi desu ka?). A healing landscape series goes to C6-1; a band or idol arc that drives the plot goes to C6-4 or C6-5.
leaves.aliases: CGDCT; moe slice of life; kirara-kei
leaves.see: C6-1 Iyashikei; C10-4 School Comedy Anime
leaves.axis: by what the girls gather around: the classroom, a hobby or club, a café or job, a supernatural roommate, moe militaria, cat-girls and fanservice

leaves.label: Club Activity Anime (Bukatsu)
leaves.defn: A series built around an after-school or university club (bukatsu) whose activity is a hobby rather than a sport or a band: otaku circles, film-making, diving, odd societies (Genshiken, Eizouken ni wa Te wo Dasu na!, Grand Blue). A sports club goes to C7; a girls' hobby ensemble with no arc goes to C6-2.
leaves.see: C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things; C10-4 School Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Idol Anime
leaves.defn: A series whose protagonists train, debut and perform as Japanese-style pop idols (Love Live!, The iDOLM@STER, Uta no Prince-sama, Zombieland Saga). A rock band goes to C6-5; a thriller set in the idol industry goes to C8-2.
leaves.see: C6-5 Music Anime; C6-6 Performing Arts Anime
leaves.axis: by who the idols are: girl units, boy units, and genre hybrids that put idols in a horror, comedy or fantasy frame

leaves.label: Music Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film about making music as players, where rehearsal and performance are the dramatic spine (Beck, Hibike! Euphonium, Shigatsu wa Kimi no Uso, Bocchi the Rock!). Idol units go to C6-4; staged theatre and rakugo go to C6-6; a cute-girls band ensemble without a performance arc (K-On!) stays in C6-2.
leaves.see: C6-4 Idol Anime; C6-6 Performing Arts Anime
leaves.axis: by the ensemble and repertoire: rock and pop bands, concert bands and orchestras, classical soloists, and other scenes (jazz, rap battle, traditional instruments)

leaves.label: Performing Arts Anime
leaves.defn: A series about stage performers outside pop music: actors, revue and theatre troupes, rakugo storytellers, voice actors and dancers (Shouwa Genroku Rakugo Shinjuu, Kageki Shoujo!!, Glass no Kamen, Shoujo Kageki Revue Starlight). Idols go to C6-4; competitive ballroom goes to C7-11.
leaves.see: C6-4 Idol Anime; C6-5 Music Anime

leaves.label: Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.defn: A series in which preparing, serving or eating food is the engine of each episode: cooking battles, home cooking, gourmet drinking and fantasy restaurants (Shokugeki no Souma, Amaama to Inazuma, Isekai Shokudou, Wakako-zake). A café used only as a backdrop for cute girls goes to C6-2.
leaves.aliases: Gurume anime; food anime; cooking manga adaptations

leaves.label: Workplace Anime (Oshigoto)
leaves.defn: A series about doing a job, in which the profession's routines, deadlines and colleagues drive the story (Shirobako, Working!!, Aggressive Retsuko, Bakuman.). A café that only frames a cute-girls ensemble goes to C6-2; a restaurant whose dishes drive it goes to C6-7.
leaves.aliases: Oshigoto anime; occupational anime; work comedy
leaves.see: C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things; C6-7 Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.axis: by the trade: creative industries (anime, manga, games, voice acting), service and retail, office and salaryman life, other professions and trades

leaves.label: Family Slice of Life (Home Drama)
leaves.defn: An episodic series about a household — a single parent, a found family, siblings or a new marriage — whose daily care and quarrels are the story (Usagi Drop, Kakushigoto, Gakuen Babysitters, Ani ni Tsukeru Kusuri wa Nai!). Arc-driven family films go to C8-7; family comedy for small children goes to C11-1.
leaves.aliases: Hōmu dorama; parenting anime; ikuji anime
leaves.see: C8-7 Coming-of-Age Drama Anime; C11-1 Kodomo Anime
leaves.axis: by the household: parents and found families, siblings and household comedies, supernatural and fantasy households

leaves.label: Monster Girl Anime
leaves.defn: A slice-of-life or comedy series in which a dragon, demi-human, mermaid, vampire or other non-human girl lives in the human everyday (Kobayashi-san Chi no Maid Dragon, Demi-chan wa Kataritai, Shinryaku! Ika Musume). A fanservice harem of monster girls goes to C10-9; a demon lord working a day job goes to C10-6.
leaves.see: C10-6 Fantasy Comedy Anime; C10-9 Harem Anime

subs.label: Sports & Game Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the sport or game that is played.

leaves.label: Baseball Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series or film whose contests are baseball games, typically high-school Koushien drives (Major, Touch, Diamond no Ace, Ookiku Furikabutte). A baseball con-game thriller such as One Outs stays here with see-also C8-3.

leaves.label: Football Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series whose contests are association football or another football code — rugby, American football — or a kindred contact team game (Captain Tsubasa, Inazuma Eleven, Blue Lock, Eyeshield 21).
leaves.see: C7-1 Baseball Anime; C7-3 Basketball Anime
leaves.axis: by code: association football first, then rugby, gridiron and other contact team games

leaves.label: Basketball Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series or film whose contests are basketball games (Slam Dunk, Kuroko no Basket, Ahiru no Sora). Franchise omake and NG reels stay with their series.

leaves.label: Volleyball Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series whose contests are volleyball, indoor or beach (Haikyuu!!, Attack No.1, Harukana Receive). The Attack No.1 shoujo spokon is the canonical ancestor; franchise specials stay with their series.

leaves.label: Racket Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series whose contests are played with a racket or paddle: tennis, badminton, table tennis (Tennis no Oujisama, Baby Steps, Ping Pong the Animation, Hanebado!). Gag shorts such as Teekyuu go to C10-1.

leaves.label: Combat Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about a ring or mat contest — boxing, pro wrestling, judo, sumo, kendo (Ashita no Joe, Hajime no Ippo, Megalo Box, Yawara!). Fantasy fighting tournaments go to C1.

leaves.label: Racing Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series or film whose contests are races on wheels — street and touge racing, circuit and formula racing, road cycling (Initial D, Mach GoGoGo, Redline, Yowamushi Pedal).
leaves.axis: by vehicle and venue: street and touge racing, circuit and formula racing, road cycling

leaves.label: Swimming & Water Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about swimming, diving, surfing or racing on water (Free!, Dive!!, Wave!! Surfing Yappe!!). A fanservice swim-club series goes to C10-10; a diving-club comedy to C6-3.

leaves.label: Winter & Ice Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about figure skating, ice hockey or other sports on ice (Yuri!!! on Ice, Medalist, Skate-Leading Stars). Idol series that only use skating go to C6-4.

leaves.label: Horse Racing Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about thoroughbred racing, literal or through horse-girls (Uma Musume: Pretty Derby, Gunjou no Fanfare). Small, but a recognised franchise canon.

leaves.label: Individual Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about a sport scored person by person rather than by a ball team: track and running, gymnastics and cheer, archery and golf, climbing and skating, shooting and airsoft (Kaze ga Tsuyoku Fuiteiru, Tsurune, Birdie Wing, SK8 the Infinity). Ball team sports go to C7-1 to C7-4.
leaves.see: C7-5 Racket Sports Anime; C7-6 Combat Sports Anime
leaves.axis: by discipline: track and running, gymnastics cheer and dance sport, archery golf and precision sports, climbing skating and extreme sports, shooting airsoft and tankery

leaves.label: Board Game & Mind Sport Anime
leaves.defn: A series about competitive play at a traditional table game — go, shogi, karuta, mahjong — or a quiz (Hikaru no Go, Chihayafuru, Saki, 3-gatsu no Lion). Gambling for ruinous stakes goes to C8-3.
leaves.see: C7-13 Card Game Anime; C8-3 Death Game Anime
leaves.axis: by the game: go and shogi, karuta, mahjong, other tabletop and quiz games

leaves.label: Card Game Anime
leaves.defn: A series whose battles are trading-card-game duels, usually a tie-in to the card game itself (Yu-Gi-Oh!, Cardfight!! Vanguard, Selector Infected WIXOSS). Spinning-top and figure battles go to C11-3.

leaves.label: Esports & Video Game Anime
leaves.defn: A series about competitive video-gaming or puzzle contests played as a sport (Quanzhi Gaoshou, Bokura no Ame-iro Protocol, Phi Brain). Isekai trapped in a game world go to C3.

subs.label: Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the dramatic engine: a puzzle to solve, a mind under pressure, a deadly game, crime, history and war, or an emotional arc.

leaves.label: Detective & Mystery Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film built on cases to solve: a detective, sleuthing student or investigator reasons from clues to a solution (Meitantei Conan, Hyouka, Kusuriya no Hitorigoto, Gosick). A thriller where the mind duel matters more than the solution goes to C8-2.
leaves.see: C8-2 Psychological Thriller Anime; C8-4 Crime & Gangster Anime
leaves.axis: by who solves and what kind of puzzle: the boy-detective franchise, teen and school sleuths, everyday mysteries, occult and supernatural detectives, period mysteries, procedural and sci-fi investigators

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film whose suspense comes from minds under pressure — duels of wits, unstable identity, manipulation and paranoia (Death Note, Perfect Blue, Monster, Zankyou no Terror). A deadly game with rules goes to C8-3; supernatural dread goes to C9.
leaves.see: C8-3 Death Game Anime; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by the source of the pressure: duels of wits and manipulation, fractured identity and perception, conspiracy and science-fiction paranoia, dark adolescence

leaves.label: Death Game Anime
leaves.defn: A series in which characters are forced into a game whose losers die, are ruined or enslaved — battle royales, survival games and high-stakes gambling (Kaiji, Mirai Nikki, Danganronpa, Kakegurui). An open-ended mind duel without a game goes to C8-2.
leaves.aliases: Death game; desu gēmu; battle royale anime; gambling anime
leaves.see: C8-2 Psychological Thriller Anime; C7-12 Board Game & Mind Sport Anime
leaves.axis: by the stakes: gambling and mind-game contests first, then death games and battle royales

leaves.label: Crime & Gangster Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film whose protagonists are criminals, thieves, gangsters or the cops who chase them (Lupin III, 91 Days, Baccano!, Banana Fish). A case-solving detective goes to C8-1.
leaves.axis: by who is at the centre: gentleman thieves and con artists, mafia and gangsters, cops and period lawmen

leaves.label: War Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film about a real or alternate-history war, its soldiers or its civilians (Hotaru no Haka, Hadashi no Gen, Kono Sekai no Katasumi ni, Kingdom). Space and mecha wars go to C2.
leaves.see: C8-6 Historical Drama Anime; C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime
leaves.axis: by front: home front and civilian experience, battlefield and campaign epics, espionage and alternate-history war

leaves.label: Historical Drama Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film set in a recreated historical period, whose drama comes from that period's people and politics (Vinland Saga, Versailles no Bara, Heike Monogatari, Golden Kamuy). A war-centred story goes to C8-5.
leaves.axis: by setting: Japanese period drama (jidaigeki), Chinese historical drama, European and other historical drama

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Drama Anime
leaves.defn: A drama, series or film whose subject is growing up — first loss, friendship, vocation, identity — resolved through an emotional arc (Ano Hi Mita Hana no Namae, Koe no Katachi, Sora yori mo Tooi Basho, Blue Period). Episodic daily life goes to C6; a romance-led story goes to C5.
leaves.see: C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime; C5 Romance Anime
leaves.axis: by the arc: school-youth drama, grief and healing, vocation and adult lives, family and growing-up films, disaster and survival

leaves.label: Melodrama Anime
leaves.defn: A drama built to make the audience cry — terminal illness, lost memory, doomed love, shoujo hardship — often from nakige visual novels (Violet Evergarden, Little Busters!, Candy Candy, Kokoro Connect). A quieter coming-of-age arc goes to C8-7.

leaves.label: Medical Drama Anime
leaves.defn: A series about doctors, rescuers or the body as a hospital whose cases drive each episode (Black Jack, Young Black Jack, Megumi no Daigo).

leaves.label: Art Anime
leaves.defn: An auteur or independent work valued for form over story — wordless, painterly or allegorical (Tenshi no Tamago, Kanashimi no Belladonna, Tsumiki no Ie, Mind Game).
leaves.see: A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde; C14 Animated Short

subs.label: Horror Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of the dread: ghosts and curses, the village, the vampire, the dead, the body, or dread played for laughs.

leaves.label: Ghost Story Anime (Kaidan)
leaves.defn: A horror series or film whose terror is a ghost, curse or urban legend in the tradition of the Japanese kaidan (Yami Shibai, Jigoku Shoujo, Another, Gakkou no Kaidan). A village cult or rural curse goes to C9-2.
leaves.aliases: Kaidan; J-horror anime; urban legend horror
leaves.see: C9-2 Folk Horror Anime; C9-6 Comedy Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by form of haunting: anthologies and urban-legend shorts, haunted schools, curses and vengeance, occult investigators and exorcists

leaves.label: Folk Horror Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series set in an isolated village or community whose customs, gods or rites are the danger (Higurashi no Naku Koro ni, Hikaru ga Shinda Natsu, Ookamikakushi).

leaves.label: Vampire Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series or film whose monster is the vampire (Blood+, Shiki, Kyuuketsuhime Miyu). Vampire romcoms go to C10-6.

leaves.label: Zombie Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series or film about the walking dead and the outbreak they cause (Highschool of the Dead, Biohazard: Degeneration, Gakkougurashi!).

leaves.label: Body Horror & Cosmic Horror Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series or film whose dread is the mutated body, the grotesque (ero guro) or an incomprehensible cosmic order (Uzumaki, Itou Junji: Collection, Elfen Lied, Pupa).

leaves.label: Comedy Horror Anime
leaves.defn: A series whose ghosts, curses or zombies are played for laughs as much as frights (Mieruko-chan, Zom 100, Jigoku Sensei Nube). Pure gag series with a monster mascot go to C10.

subs.label: Comedy Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the comic engine: absurd gag, parody, spin-off, school life, otaku life, a fantasy or science-fiction premise, action, harem and fanservice.

leaves.label: Gag Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is the gag itself — non sequitur, slapstick, manzai timing, satire — with little or no plot (Nichijou, Poputepipikku, Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo, Sayonara Zetsubou Sensei). Parody of a named work goes to C10-2; a spin-off of a non-comedy series goes to C10-3.
leaves.see: C10-2 Parody Anime; C10-4 School Comedy Anime
leaves.axis: by how the gag works: surreal and absurdist, slapstick and manzai, satirical, short-form and flash

leaves.label: Parody Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose jokes depend on the audience knowing the genre, franchise or history it mocks (Gintama, Hayate no Gotoku!, Haiyore! Nyaruko-san, Hetalia). A chibi spin-off of one specific series goes to C10-3.
leaves.see: C10-3 Chibi Spin-off Anime; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by the target: jidaigeki and shounen (Gintama), genre and media parody, magical-girl and tokusatsu parody, national and historical parody

leaves.label: Chibi Spin-off Anime
leaves.defn: A short comedy spin-off of a (usually non-comedy) series, often drawn super-deformed: theatre shorts, crossovers of several franchises, omake and picture dramas (Isekai Quartet, Carnival Phantasm, Sword Art Offline, Shingeki! Kyojin Chuugakkou). An original parody goes to C10-2.
leaves.axis: by form: chibi theatres and four-panel shorts, multi-franchise crossovers, omake specials and picture dramas

leaves.label: School Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose jokes come from school life — classmates, the student council, a club, a teacher — rather than from a romance (Baka to Test to Shoukanjuu, Seitokai Yakuindomo, Tonari no Seki-kun, Saiki Kusuo no Psi-nan). A school romcom goes to C5; a cute-girls ensemble goes to C6-2.
leaves.see: C5 Romance Anime; C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things
leaves.axis: by the school setting: student council and club comedies, classroom and deskmate comedies, delinquents and teachers, superpowered students, elementary-school comedies

leaves.label: Otaku Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy about otaku life — fandom, games, doujinshi, cosplay, shut-ins and their embarrassments (Himouto! Umaru-chan, Watashi ga Motenai no wa Dou Kangaetemo Omaera ga Warui!, Otaku no Video). An otaku club arc goes to C6-3.
leaves.see: C6-3 Club Activity Anime; C10-2 Parody Anime

leaves.label: Fantasy Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose premise is a fantasy being or world — demons, gods, vampires, youkai, isekai heroes — dropped into absurd situations (Hataraku Maou-sama!, Hoozuki no Reitetsu, Saint Oniisan, Kono Healer, Mendokusai). A monster girl's quiet daily life goes to C6-10.
leaves.see: C6-10 Monster Girl Anime; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by premise: demons and gods next door, vampires youkai and spirits, isekai and RPG-world comedy, witches and magic

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose premise is science fiction — aliens, robots, time travel, space crews (Urusei Yatsura, Keroro Gunsou, Space Dandy, Hinamatsuri).
leaves.axis: by the science-fiction premise: alien visitors and invaders, robots androids and the body, space crews and space opera, time travel and other premises

leaves.label: Action Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy built on fights, missions or chases — martial artists, spies, ninja, cops, delinquents (Ranma 1/2, Spy x Family, Kyou kara Ore wa!!, Taiho Shichau zo).
leaves.axis: by who fights: martial artists, spies assassins and ninja, delinquents and yakuza, cops and prison comedies

leaves.label: Harem Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy in which one protagonist is surrounded by several romantic candidates, usually with fanservice (To LOVE-Ru, High School DxD, Rosario to Vampire, Sekirei). Without the harem structure, fanservice comedy goes to C10-10; a romance-led story goes to C5.
leaves.see: C10-10 Ecchi Anime; C5 Romance Anime
leaves.axis: by premise: supernatural and demon harems, alien and science-fiction harems, fantasy-world and battle harems, domestic and school harems

leaves.label: Ecchi Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy or action series whose main appeal is sexual fanservice short of explicit sex (Prison School, Queen's Blade, Getsuyoubi no Tawawa, Keijo!!!!!!!!). With a harem structure it goes to C10-9; explicit erotica is out of scope.
leaves.see: C10-9 Harem Anime; A15 Erotic Film
leaves.axis: by vehicle of the fanservice: fanservice battle series, ecchi comedies, fetish and pin-up shorts, sports fanservice, mature and taboo ecchi

subs.label: Children's & Family Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the kind of children's property: everyday family anime, monster-partner franchise, toy tie-in, literary classic, or pre-war film.

leaves.label: Kodomo Anime
leaves.defn: Anime made for young children and the family audience: household comedies, animal tales and gentle fantasy (Doraemon, Crayon Shin-chan, Sazae-san, Gamba no Bouken). Monster-collecting franchises go to C11-2.
leaves.see: C11-2 Monster-Collecting Anime; C6-9 Family Slice of Life
leaves.axis: by mode: everyday family comedy, animal tales and fables, fantasy and adventure for children

leaves.label: Monster-Collecting Anime
leaves.defn: A children's franchise in which kids befriend, collect and battle with monster partners, tied to games (Pokemon, Digimon Adventure, Youkai Watch).
leaves.axis: by franchise: Pokemon, Digimon, other monster-partner franchises

leaves.label: Toy & Game Tie-in Anime
leaves.defn: A children's series made to sell a toy line or video game, whose battles are fought with the product (Bakuten Shoot Beyblade, Bakugan Battle Brawlers, Medarot, Rockman.EXE). Trading-card duels go to C7-13.

leaves.label: World Masterpiece Theater
leaves.defn: Nippon Animation's Sekai Meisaku Gekijou adaptations of Western children's classics and the kindred literary adaptations of the period (Akage no Anne, Flanders no Inu, Haha wo Tazunete Sanzenri, Muumin).

leaves.label: Early Japanese Animation
leaves.defn: Japanese animation from the silent era to the early 1960s, before television anime: folk-tale shorts, wartime propaganda, post-war shorts (Namakura Gatana, Momotarou: Umi no Shinpei, Kobutori).
